baseline: The player is yellow; white score popups are not targets. Objects move horizontally; UP/DOWN changes rows. Anticipate motion during the response delay and current held action. Intercept nearby safe collectibles, avoid lyres. Once aligned, release vertical motion. Use recent applied actions to maintain a maneuver unless a new hazard requires changing it.
retreat_v1: The player is yellow; white score popups are not targets. Objects move horizontally; UP/DOWN changes rows. Anticipate motion during the response delay and current held action. Intercept nearby safe collectibles, avoid lyres. Once aligned, release vertical motion. Use recent applied actions to maintain a maneuver unless a new hazard requires changing it. When a lyre in your row approaches, do not run toward it. Prefer horizontal retreat away from it when neighboring rows are threatened. Change rows only after the crossing path has cleared; use a diagonal away from the threat when it adds clearance. Judge this at response arrival, not at screenshot time. Check the whole crossing path, not just its endpoint.
retreat_score_v2: The player is yellow; white score popups are not targets. Objects move horizontally; UP/DOWN changes rows. Anticipate motion during the response delay and current held action. Intercept nearby safe collectibles, avoid lyres. Once aligned, release vertical motion. Use recent applied actions to maintain a maneuver unless a new hazard requires changing it. When a lyre in your row approaches, do not run toward it. Prefer horizontal retreat away from it when neighboring rows are threatened. Change rows only after the crossing path has cleared; use a diagonal away from the threat when it adds clearance. Judge this at response arrival, not at screenshot time. Check the whole crossing path, not just its endpoint. Among safe actions, intercept reachable collectibles, including by staying in their row and moving toward them. Do not chase a departing item that will leave before interception. White score text is already earned, not a target. If no useful item is reachable, waiting or returning toward the center can preserve options; do not change rows without a safety or scoring purpose.
maneuver_v3: The player is yellow. Identify pink pronged lyres as hazards and round collectibles as targets; white numbers are already earned score. Use the newest image for current positions and older images for motion. Predict positions when the response arrives, including the held action. If a lyre approaches in your row, take an empty adjacent row when the entire crossing is clear. If both neighboring rows contain lyres, first retreat horizontally away from the approaching same-row lyre, then change rows after a crossing clears. Never move head-on toward that lyre. If currently safe, do not invent a dodge: pursue a reachable real collectible, including by changing rows through a safe gap. If a neighboring lyre is crossing your horizontal position, enter behind it after it passes; do not move toward it along its path. Release vertical motion after one row and reobserve. Do not chase a departing collectible that will leave before interception. When no collectible is reachable, wait or return toward the center to preserve room on both sides.
active_escape_v4: The controllable player is the yellow sprite inside the purple playfield; yellow icons below it are lives. Pink pronged lyres are hazards, round collectibles are targets, and white numbers are earned score. Predict positions at action arrival using the chronological images, response delay, and held action. Decision order: If a lyre approaches in your current row, choose an active escape, not NOOP. If both neighboring rows contain lyres, retreat horizontally: approaching lyre on your right means LEFT; approaching lyre on your left means RIGHT. Change rows after a crossing clears. If a neighboring row is empty and the whole crossing is clear, escape into it; add horizontal motion away from the current-row enemy when it improves clearance. Never move head-on toward a current-row lyre. If currently safe, do not invent a dodge. Intercept a reachable real collectible, including through a safe row change. Enter behind a neighboring lyre after it passes, instead of moving toward it along its path. Release vertical motion after one row and reobserve. Ignore departing collectibles that leave before interception. If no useful item is reachable, wait or return toward the center.
shape_escape_v5: The controllable player is the yellow sprite inside the purple playfield; yellow icons below it are lives. Lyres are tall, pale salmon-pink, hollow fork or bracket shapes. Collectibles are shorter, darker red, compact rounded objects with a dark center. Distinguish silhouette and color before treating an object as an enemy: not every red moving object is a lyre. White numbers are earned score, not targets. Predict positions at action arrival using the chronological images, response delay, and held action. Decision order: If a lyre approaches in your current row, choose an active escape, not NOOP. If both neighboring rows contain lyres, retreat horizontally: approaching lyre on your right means LEFT; approaching lyre on your left means RIGHT. Change rows after a crossing clears. If a neighboring row is empty and the whole crossing is clear, escape into it; add horizontal motion away from the current-row enemy when it improves clearance. Never move head-on toward a current-row lyre. If currently safe, do not invent a dodge. Intercept a reachable real collectible, including through a safe row change. Enter behind a neighboring lyre after it passes, instead of moving toward it along its path. Release vertical motion after one row and reobserve. Ignore departing collectibles that leave before interception. If no useful item is reachable, wait or return toward the center. In a row containing an approaching collectible and no lyre, intercept the collectible instead of dodging away from it.
priority_escape_v6: The player is the yellow sprite inside the purple field, not the life icons below. Use the newest image for object identity and position; earlier images only estimate motion of the same object. Lyres are tall pale-pink hollow forks; collectibles are short dark-red rounded objects. White numbers are earned score. Predict action-arrival positions using delay and held motion. Priority 1: escape an approaching lyre in your current row. If BOTH adjacent rows contain lyres, retreat now: lyre to your RIGHT -> LEFT (3); lyre to your LEFT -> RIGHT (2). Do not choose NOOP just because contact is not yet immediate. If an adjacent row is empty and the entire crossing is clear, escape into it, diagonally away from the enemy when useful. Priority 2: without a current-row lyre, intercept a reachable real collectible; do not dodge away from it. Enter a neighboring row behind a passing lyre, not toward it. Release vertical motion after one row and reobserve. Ignore departing items that leave before interception. With no reachable item or threat, wait or return toward the center.
